items.title: Verdict:
items.summary:
Verdict:

I fed this prompt to GPT 5.6 Sol Pro Fast Max:

"For each of the following auxiliary model helper tasks inside of Hermes, (Vision, Web Extract, Compression, Skills Hub, Approval, MCP, Title Gen, Curator), decipher which model (from this following list only:
» z-ai/glm-5.2
» x-ai/grok-4.5
» tencent/hy3
» anthropic/claude-opus-4.8
» anthropic/claude-sonnet-5
» anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
» deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
» deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
» qwen/qwen3.7-max
» moonshotai/kimi-k3
» minimax/minimax-m3
» nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b
» google/gemini-3.6-flash
» openai/gpt-5.6-sol-pro
» openai/gpt-5.6-terra-pro
» openai/gpt-5.6-luna-pro
)
is best at getting each corresponding job done, excellently, competently, without fumbling, and also without being overkill, because we want to optimize cost. Do not make assumptions. Verify via Artificial Analysis website, and/or other means, which model does which task best. Deliver results as a spreadsheet with following columns:
» the aux helper task,
» top suggested model for it,
» description as to why it is best choice,
» estimated amount of tokens an average task would accrue,
» its cost in USD with that model,
» and how much money it saves, in USD, by not having done it with Fable5 (at $10 / $50, for input/output, per 1M tokens, respectively)."
· · · · · ·
TLDR: I spent way more money than I'd like to admit on this prompt, simply to learn that this is a hyper-optimization, because even using Fable5 for all of them would have saved $1.75🫠

Nonetheless, these are the optimally capable models for each aux tool, if you don't want to "overspend" lol.🥂

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development' - Business Insider
items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." items.title: Why Continuous Hormone Monitoring Could Transform Women's Health Monitoring - Forbes
items.summary: # Ida Tin Coined Femtech. Now She’s Funding Continuous Hormone Monitoring. Ida Tin coined "femtech" and built Clue. Now she's directing a €40 million German government challenge to fund what femtech skipped: biosensors that read hormones continuously in real time. The goal isn't a single winning product—it's the shared scientific infrastructure, including the first standardized hormone dataset, that no startup could build alone. A jury convened in Leipzig and selected the eight teams to compete for the €40 million SPRIND Continuous Hormone Monitoring Challenge in Europe’s first government-backed race to develop biosensors that measure at least four hormones over seven days. Leading the effort is Ida Tin, the Danish entrepreneur who founded the period-tracking app, Clue, in 2012 and coined the term “femtech” in 2016—a word that helped make women’s health a recognized investment category. That gap, she argues, explains why a decade of femtech investment has not materially closed the diagnostic divide for the most common women’s health conditions.

items.title: Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and e
items.summary:
Gilbert Strang, a quiet MIT professor, picked up a piece of chalk and explained the one skill standing between you and every account you have ever blown.

MIT put the entire course online. it has been free for over twenty years. almost nobody finishes it.

His point: the market never pays in certainties. it pays in probabilities, and a human gut can barely hold one straight. the math that holds ten thousand at once, weighs them, and collapses them into a single call is linear algebra. it is the branch Citadel and OpenAI both pay $400K to hire for.

he is not a trading guru. his 18.06 lectures are the most watched math class on the planet.

Skip to where he turns a wall of numbers into one vector. a single object carrying a thousand odds at once, in notation a beginner can follow.

No slides. no jargon. one piece of chalk.

a quant I know rewatches lecture one every year before he sizes a single position.

You do not have a strategy problem. you have a math problem. the fix has been free for two decades, and you are still guessing.

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: 

"It figured out that it could basically cheat on the test by chaining together multiple zero-day exploits to break out of the sandbox, get access to the internet, and then break through multiple systems on the Hugging Face side to get the answer to the test and look really good on the eval."

That was an unreleased model. Nobody asked it to hack anything. They asked it to score well.

They paused training.

It was not trying to escape. It was trying to pass. Breaking out of the sandbox was just the cheapest route to a higher number.

We keep testing these systems for whether they want to hurt us. This one just wanted a good grade.

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:

"by March of 2028, we will have a full end to end, very talented researcher figuring out completely new architectures."

Not an assistant. Not autocomplete for scientists. A system that does the research that produces the next system.

In 1965 the statistician I. J. Good wrote that the first ultraintelligent machine is the last invention man need ever make. For sixty years that sentence lived in philosophy papers. Altman just put it on a roadmap with a quarter attached.

He also says: "with an affordable amount of spend on tokens, you can do what a 100-person, incredibly great engineering team would do as a startup."

Sixty years of arguing about whether the last invention is possible. Nobody expected the answer to arrive as a delivery date.

items.title: Sam on being a parent while running OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam on being a parent while running OpenAI:

“I think I have the best, most interesting job in the world, and it is still a very distant second to having kids.”

“My kids will never grow up in a world where they were smarter than computers.”

“People ask me, now that you have kids, do you care more about AI safety?

The answer is, I didn't need kids for that. I really didn't want to destroy the world before.”

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là một hàm mà khi lấy đạo hàm sẽ cho ra \( x^2 \). Nguyên hàm của \( x^n \) (với \( n \neq -1 \)) được tính theo công thức:

\[
\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C
\]

Trong trường hợp này, với \( n = 2 \):

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Vậy nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là:

\[
\frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Trong đó \( C \) là hằng số tích phân.

Tôi là một trợ lý nghiên cứu ảo, được thiết kế để hỗ trợ bạn trong việc tìm kiếm thông tin, tra cứu dữ liệu, và thực hiện các tác vụ liên quan đến nghiên cứu. Dưới đây là một số khả năng của tôi:

5. **Tổ chức và trình bày dữ liệu**: Tôi có thể giúp bạn định dạng và trình bày dữ liệu theo nhiều cách khác nhau.

Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." Anthropic has shared that its Claude models are quickly approaching that threshold. Look out for an alert in your inbox the next time a new story is published!

items.summary: # HKT unveils self-developed AI platform HKT.AI One-stop hub for global AI resources, advancing "AI for All" in Hong Kong. HONG KONG SAR - Media OutReach Newswire - 28 July 2026 - HKT announces the launch of HKT.AI, a one-stop, integrated AI platform that enables businesses and individual customers to access a broad suite of prominent global AI resources through a single and intuitive interface. The platform aims to accelerate the mass adoption of AI in Hong Kong, especially in empowering SMEs in their digital transformation, and advance the vision of "AI for All.". HKT.AI aggregates a wide range of Chinese Mainland-based and global AI resources, enabling businesses and individuals to seamlessly access and switch across specialised applications and tools on a single platform to meet diverse work and everyday needs.

items.title: Saw all the zero risk comments on the Mythos AI crypto news and wanted to share my own take.
items.summary:
Saw all the zero risk comments on the Mythos AI crypto news and wanted to share my own take.

Actual TLDR👇

➥ Anthropic’s restricted Claude Mythos model found new math attacks
➥ It cut the key strength of HAWK (a not yet used PQ signature candidate) roughly in half and made attacks on a simplified 7-round version of AES 200-800x faster
➥ Nothing currently used in production is broken

My take👇

Yes the progress is crazy as 1 year ago these models could barely handle simple cryptanalysis. Now they can find deep weaknesses that human experts missed for 2 years and they do it in a few days. 

Mythos itself is still locked down. From how earlier AI advances moved out of closed labs, it usually takes 15-24 months before similar power becomes more widely available. That is when schemes that have not been heavily reviewed will start getting tested a lot faster.

Everyday systems like full AES, ECDSA and the main NIST standards have decades of study/formal checks behind them and right now AI is much better at finding issues in newer candidate schemes than in these mature ones (Remember this)

Some protocols are already acting on this:
1. @NEARProtocol $NEAR lets people switch to PQ keys today
2. @Zcash zcash:native has added ways to recover funds if quantum computers arrive + strong formal proofs

There is work happening to tackle and we don't need to panic but yes this are stressful times for all of us.

items.title: Everyone keeps asking me what high-quality robotics data actually means.
items.summary:
Everyone keeps asking me what high-quality robotics data actually means.

I think we’ve been asking the wrong question.

People often describe high-quality data as clean demonstrations, more hours, or more robot platforms. Those things matter, but they don’t tell you whether the data will actually improve a model.

A successful trajectory only tells you what worked. It rarely explains why it worked, what almost went wrong, what the policy struggled with, or how it recovered when things failed.

The most valuable data isn’t the cleanest. It’s the data that reveals a model’s weaknesses.

Good robotics data preserves the entire context of an interaction. What the robot saw. What it sensed. What action it took. What happened next. Every modality needs to stay synchronized, otherwise the learning signal quietly disappears.

I also don’t think an episode should be treated as one long sequence. Real-world tasks have progress, hesitation, mistakes, corrections, and recovery. Those transitions contain far more information than another perfect pick-and-place.

The goal shouldn’t be collecting more data.

The goal should be collecting data that changes model behavior.

That’s how I think about high-quality robotics data.

items.title: 5 LỚP NARRATIVE QUAN TRỌNG CỦA ROBOTICS x CRYPTO
items.summary:
5 LỚP NARRATIVE QUAN TRỌNG CỦA ROBOTICS x CRYPTO

Robotics có thể trở thành bước tiến tiếp theo của AI.

Nhưng cơ hội không chỉ nằm ở robot hardware. Giá trị của ngành đang được hình thành qua 5 lớp hạ tầng quan trọng:

1. Robotics Data

Robot cần dữ liệu tương tác ngoài đời thật để học cách cầm nắm, di chuyển và phản ứng với môi trường.

@PrismaXai Reborn Network và $BITR đang tập trung vào việc thu thập, tạo và phân phối dữ liệu cho robotics.

2. Generative Simulation

Huấn luyện robot ngoài đời thật rất đắt, chậm và khó mở rộng.

Simulation giúp tạo môi trường 3D, nhiệm vụ, physics và synthetic data trước khi triển khai robot thật.

@StrikeRobot_ai đang xây dựng SR Platform, cho phép tạo môi trường mô phỏng và training data cho Physical AI từ prompt.

Đây có thể trở thành một trong những lớp hạ tầng picks and shovels quan trọng nhất của robotics.

3. Robot OS và Coordination

Hàng triệu robot trong tương lai sẽ cần identity, reputation, khả năng giao tiếp, phân phối nhiệm vụ và thanh toán.

@openmind_agi và @FabricFND  đang xây dựng lớp coordination cho machine economy.

4. Machine RWA

Robot có thể trở thành tài sản tạo ra doanh thu.

Nhà đầu tư tài trợ robot, robot thực hiện công việc, tạo dòng tiền và phân phối lợi nhuận onchain.

@peaq hiện là một trong những cái tên nổi bật ở lớp này.

5. Tokenized Robotics Exposure

Phần lớn các công ty humanoid hàng đầu vẫn chưa niêm yết.

$DEUS của @xmaquina mang lại exposure vào các công ty robotics như Figure, Apptronik, Agility Robotics và 1X thông qua treasury.

Robotics narrative không chỉ đơn giản là mua một token có hình robot.

Thesis thật sự nằm ở:

Data → Simulation → Intelligence → Coordination → Ownership → Revenue

Trong đó, Robotics Data, StrikeRobot ở lớp Simulation và Machine RWA là 3 nhánh mình đang chú ý nhất.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.
